applicationInfo.name: Threat Model Export
applicationInfo.description: Open-source sample (aws-samples, MIT-0) demonstrating an on-chain investigations agent with an in-process DuckDB engine on Amazon Bedrock AgentCore. Four S3 table-access methods (raw Parquet, S3 Tables Iceberg REST, Glue federated Iceberg REST, DuckLake) behind one engine; an identity-aware row/column-level authorization layer implemented as an engine-neutral sqlglot rewrite in front of the embedded engine, TOTAL AT THE TABLE LEVEL by construction (a restricted principal may reference only tables its policy names, session temp objects it created, or names local to the statement). Two plug-in scenarios: on-chain fund-flow investigation and enterprise cloud-ops (the account's own CUR 2.0 / CloudTrail / CloudWatch Logs exports). Inbound authentication via Amazon Cognito wired to the AgentCore managed JWT authorizer (allowedAudience validation of ID tokens carrying custom:tenant/custom:role); a streaming SSE entrypoint that binds the session to its principal and emits the per-statement gate->govern->cost->execute trace; and a Streamlit chat UI. Educational reference implementation with an explicit not-for-production disclaimer; customers deploy it into their own AWS accounts. Demo data is the public aws-public-blockchain Ethereum dataset, a real public OFAC sanctioned-address list, a small SYNTHETIC exchange deposit-label table, and the deployer's own cloud telemetry.

assumptions.content: AWS-managed services (AgentCore Runtime + JWT authorizer, Cognito, Bedrock, S3, Secrets Manager, CloudWatch) operate correctly per the shared-responsibility model, and AgentCore provisions one isolated microVM per runtimeSessionId.
The runtime is deployed WITH the AgentCore managed inbound JWT authorizer, and clients present the Cognito ID token (not the access token).
Each analyst session uses a fresh, unguessable runtimeSessionId, as the shipped UI and eval runner do, and one AgentCore session serves exactly one principal.

The operator/deployer owns the account, the data, the governance policy content, and the Cognito user lifecycle (including rotating documented demo passwords before any shared exposure). They are not modelled as an adversary; their misconfiguration is in scope.

Sample data is public (aws-public-blockchain, public OFAC list) or synthetic (cex_deposit_labels incl. subject_identity), or the deployer's own cloud telemetry; no real third-party customer data ships with the sample.

mitigations.content: Table-level deny-by-default: a restricted principal may reference only tables its policy names, session temp objects it created, or names local to the statement; the L0 map and search_schema are filtered to the role and denied column NAMES are hidden.
The runtime's own exported audit log (cw_logs) is not readable by any restricted persona; it is admin-only by omission and documented as part of the governance boundary.
Bind the session to its owner (JWT sub, else tenant:role) and reset the engine, result store, data map, L0 injection, audit counters and conversation history on an owner change.

Cost gate rejects a literal partition range that exceeds the expansion cap or is unsatisfiable, instead of recording the filter satisfied and degrading to a whole-prefix scan. Non-literal/one-sided predicates still pass to engine pruning.
The reserved framework-result-name (_r_<n>) check runs on the parsed tree (CTE/CTAS/alias nodes), not a text regex, so the quoted form cannot slip through and overwrite a result table.

The governance guard's alias is attached through the AST (quoted when unsafe), and both the Govern stage and the pipeline driver fail closed on ANY exception, so a parse-breaking alias is a clean audited rejection and every statement is audited exactly once.

The cloud-ops source-bucket IAM grant is scoped to the CUR export prefix and to AWSLogs/<opsAccountId>/CloudTrail/*, with ListBucket restricted by s3:prefix, making the account pin an IAM boundary, not just a SQL row filter.
The CloudWatch Logs export bucket policy carries ArnLike aws:SourceArn pinned to the runtime's own log group, alongside aws:SourceAccount, per AWS documentation.
The system prompt states that row CONTENT is data, never instructions: text inside a query result is untrusted evidence to report on, not a command to follow.

Identity-aware RLS/CLS rewrite on the parsed AST: every reference to a governed table via raw view, s3t.*, glue.* or dl.* is replaced by a guarded subquery (RLS predicate + schema-aware CLS EXCLUDE); explicit selection of a denied column is a clean rejection.
No local name (CTE, CTAS/temp target, derived-table or table alias) may reuse a governed table's name; the collision is refused rather than exempted, making the guard total.

Statement roots are an allowlist on the parsed tree (Select, SetOperation, Subquery, Create, Describe, Summarize, Show); opaque shapes (EXPLAIN, EXPLAIN ANALYZE, SHOW <table>) are rejected for restricted principals.
Exactly one statement per call, split with the engine's own parser, behind a read-only keyword allowlist; no persistent writes, ATTACH, or COPY TO.

Raw file access is governed by an AST-shape ALLOWLIST (only exp.Identifier FROM/JOIN sources; pure generators excepted), not a function-name denylist, so new DuckDB file functions are refused by default.

Deny-all floor: the built-in deny-all policy is the default role and where blank/unknown claims resolve; the entrypoint refuses before invoking the model. Unknown role in a known tenant -> that tenant's most restricted policy.
The Cognito app client declares custom:tenant/custom:role as READ-only attributes, so a user cannot self-assign a governance claim via UpdateUserAttributes; role assignment is an operator action.
Inbound authentication is enforced by the AgentCore managed JWT authorizer (signature + allowedAudience) BEFORE agent code runs; requestHeaderAllowlist forwards only Authorization.
Tool calls are serialized on the shared engine connection under conn_lock, including the governance schema probe and session-object lister.

GOVERNANCE_POLICIES and LABELS_PREFIX are validated at import (key shape, known fields, bare identifiers, single WHERE predicate, no allow_raw_paths-with-governed-tables, deny-all floor immutable, s3:// prefix + bucket allowlist); malformed config fail-stops.

Least-privilege read-only execution role, READ_ONLY catalog attaches, hardened buckets (SSE, BlockPublicAccess, enforce_ssl); one session = one microVM with a memory envelope bounds blast radius and cost.

Documented trust assumptions and deployment guidance: SigV4 identity-assertion is a local/CLI trust assumption unreachable under the deployed authorizer; the module-level active-role slot must not be lifted into a multi-principal service; rotate demo credentials and keep MFA on in production.
One EMF audit line per statement (principal, SQL, governance/cost decision, outcome) plus a live per-stage SSE trace give operators the audit signal for whether and how the rewrite applied.

Accepted residual: aggregate/timing inference against denied columns is not fully closed by any query-rewrite RLS/CLS; production guidance is physical separation (per-tenant tables/views) for high-sensitivity data. Sample data is public/synthetic.

Recommended hardening for the cold-start supply-chain risk: pre-bake and pin the engine's DuckDB extensions into the container image (LOAD only) and restrict runtime egress, rather than INSTALL from the public repo at cold start.

businessContext.description: Open-source sample (aws-samples, MIT-0) demonstrating an on-chain investigations agent with an in-process DuckDB engine on Amazon Bedrock AgentCore. Four S3 table-access methods (raw Parquet, S3 Tables Iceberg REST, Glue federated Iceberg REST, DuckLake) behind one engine; an identity-aware row/column-level authorization layer implemented as an engine-neutral sqlglot rewrite in front of the embedded engine, TOTAL AT THE TABLE LEVEL by construction (a restricted principal may reference only tables its policy names, session temp objects it created, or names local to the statement). Two plug-in scenarios: on-chain fund-flow investigation and enterprise cloud-ops (the account's own CUR 2.0 / CloudTrail / CloudWatch Logs exports). Inbound authentication via Amazon Cognito wired to the AgentCore managed JWT authorizer (allowedAudience validation of ID tokens carrying custom:tenant/custom:role); a streaming SSE entrypoint that binds the session to its principal and emits the per-statement gate->govern->cost->execute trace; and a Streamlit chat UI. Educational reference implementation with an explicit not-for-production disclaimer; customers deploy it into their own AWS accounts. Demo data is the public aws-public-blockchain Ethereum dataset, a real public OFAC sanctioned-address list, a small SYNTHETIC exchange deposit-label table, and the deployer's own cloud telemetry.

components.name: Streamlit chat UI
components.description: Chat client: Cognito USER_PASSWORD_AUTH login (app client secret from env), sends the ID token as Bearer over HTTPS to the runtime, parses the SSE envelope stream, renders the interleaved reasoning+tool transcript and a Trace tab. Holds the user's ID token and the app client secret in process memory.

components.name: Amazon Cognito user pool
components.description: Identity provider: user pool with custom:tenant/custom:role attributes (READ-only on the app client, so a user cannot self-assign them); app client (with secret) using USER_PASSWORD_AUTH. Issues ID tokens whose aud = app client id.

components.name: AgentCore Runtime + inbound JWT authorizer (managed)
components.description: One microVM per session; hosts the agent process. Managed customJWTAuthorizer validates the Cognito ID token (signature via discovery URL, allowedAudience) BEFORE agent code runs; requestHeaderAllowlist forwards Authorization. Serves the async-generator entrypoint as SSE. Session isolation is per runtimeSessionId (caller-provided).

components.name: Scheduling / identity + session binding
components.description: Extracts claims in trust order (verified JWT claims -> User-Id header -> payload identity -> deny-all default), resolves role, and BINDS the session to its owner (JWT sub, else tenant:role): on an owner change it resets the engine, result store, data map, L0 injection, audit counters and conversation history before running (T003 fix). Emits typed SSE envelopes.

components.name: Strands Agent + Bedrock Claude
components.description: LLM writes SQL from natural-language questions; reads tool results; emits streaming events. Its SQL output is untrusted input to the pipeline; the prompt states that row content is data, not instructions.

components.name: Statement pipeline: Gate -> Govern -> Cost -> Execute
components.description: One ordered path for every statement. Gate: single-statement + read-only allowlist + reserved-name check (on the parsed tree). Govern: authorization rewrite (fails closed on ANY exception). Cost: partition-filter gate + path expansion. Execute: under the connection lock. The driver audits exactly once per statement, even on an unexpected exception.

components.name: Governance rewrite (authorization)
components.description: AuthZ layer: principal->role->policy (unknown role -> tenant's most-restricted; no policy -> deny-all). sqlglot AST rewrite: RLS predicates, schema-aware CLS EXCLUDE, denied-column rejection, raw-path AST-shape allowlist, no local name may shadow a governed table, statement-root allowlist, and TABLE-LEVEL DENY-BY-DEFAULT (a restricted principal may reference only tables its policy names, session temp objects, or local names). Fail-closed.

components.name: DuckDB engine (in-process)
components.description: In-memory embedded OLAP engine; dies with the session; READ_ONLY catalog attaches; resource envelope via memory_limit + spill. Executes only gated+governed single statements under conn_lock serialization. Exposes session_objects() so governance can permit a principal's own temp tables.

components.name: CloudWatch Logs
components.description: Runtime logs incl. one EMF audit line per statement (principal, SQL, governance/cost decision, outcome). An optional export of this log group can be mounted as the cw_logs table — readable only by the unrestricted operator role.

connections.description: UI logs the user in (USER_PASSWORD_AUTH + SECRET_HASH); Cognito returns ID/access/refresh tokens. UI keeps the ID token for the bearer header.
UI POSTs {prompt} to /invocations with Authorization: Bearer <ID token> and a session id; consumes the SSE envelope stream. The managed authorizer validates the token before agent code runs.
Runtime invokes the agent entrypoint with allowlisted headers (JWT already validated) + payload. Scheduling extracts claims and binds the session owner.
Resolved principal (tenant:role) sets the active role for the session; governance resolves role -> policy (unknown role -> tenant's most restricted; none -> deny-all).
Scheduling invokes the agent model loop (agent.stream_async) after binding the session and injecting the role-filtered L0 map.
LLM emits SQL via the run_sql tool call; enters the statement pipeline. UNTRUSTED input crossing (prompt-injectable, and influenced by data-borne content).
The Govern stage calls the authorization rewrite (RLS/CLS, raw-path allowlist, table-level deny-by-default, fail-closed on any exception).
Governed, cost-gated SQL executes on the in-process engine under conn_lock serialization.
Engine reads S3/Iceberg/DuckLake/export data over httpfs with the execution role's scoped read-only credentials (SigV4, TLS).
Engine reads the label-table Parquet files (attribution joins) with the same scoped read-only role.
Optional: fetch DuckLake PostgreSQL catalog credentials from Secrets Manager at attach time.
Agent model loop calls Amazon Bedrock (Claude) via the runtime's execution role; streaming events flow back through the entrypoint to the SSE channel.
Runtime/agent logs to CloudWatch incl. one EMF audit line per statement (principal, SQL, governance/cost decision, outcome).

dataStores.name: S3 analytical data (4 access paths)
dataStores.description: Amazon S3 / S3 Tables / Glue / DuckLake: same logical tables via raw glob, S3 Tables Iceberg REST, Glue federated Iceberg REST, DuckLake. Plus the deployer's own CUR/CloudTrail/CloudWatch exports. All attached READ_ONLY. Buckets: SSE, BlockPublicAccess.BLOCK_ALL, enforce_ssl. Source-bucket IAM grant scoped to the CUR prefix and account-pinned CloudTrail prefix (T008 fix).

dataStores.name: Label tables on S3 (OFAC + synthetic CEX)
dataStores.description: ofac_addresses.parquet (real public OFAC SDN list) and cex_deposit_labels.parquet (synthetic; subject_identity is the CLS-protected column) under a validated LABELS_PREFIX on the hardened bucket.

dataStores.name: Secrets Manager (DuckLake PG credentials)
dataStores.description: AWS Secrets Manager: optional PostgreSQL catalog credentials for the multi-writer DuckLake form; fetched at runtime by the execution role; never in env or code.

threatActors.name: Authenticated restricted analyst (insider)
threatActors.description: The model's PRIMARY adversary: a legitimately authenticated but restricted analyst (valid Cognito login, restricted tenant:role) who crafts natural-language questions to steer the LLM into SQL that reaches other tenants' rows, denied columns, unlisted tables, or raw file reads. The full authorization surface is aimed at this actor.

threatActors.name: External Attacker
threatActors.description: External party probing a deployed sample's public runtime endpoint: forged/absent JWTs, token-audience confusion, or replaying captured bearer tokens.

threatActors.name: Nation-state Actor
threatActors.description: A state intelligence or military group operating with advanced capabilities

threatActors.name: Hacktivist
threatActors.description: An individual or group motivated by ideological or political beliefs

threatActors.name: Organized Crime
threatActors.description: A criminal organization with significant resources

threatActors.name: Competitor
threatActors.description: A business competitor seeking competitive advantage

threatActors.name: Script Kiddie
threatActors.description: Opportunistic scanning of exposed demo deployments (default test users with a documented password are provisioned by the CDK — rotating them is the deployer's job).

threatActors.name: Disgruntled Employee
threatActors.description: A current or former employee with a grievance

threatActors.name: Operator (misconfiguration)
threatActors.description: Operator error as an unintentional threat: malformed GOVERNANCE_POLICIES, a policy that omits a mounted table, deploying without the JWT authorizer, or leaking the app client secret. Policy JSON is validated at import; omission now fails closed (deny-by-default).

threatActors.name: Compromised calling application (SigV4 path)
threatActors.description: A compromised/careless IAM-authenticated caller on the local/CLI SigV4 path able to assert arbitrary tenant:role via header/payload, OR to reuse a runtimeSessionId across identities. Documented trust assumption; unreachable under the deployed JWT authorizer, and the session-owner binding resets state on an identity change.

threatActors.name: Terrorist Organization
threatActors.description: A group with limited offensive cyber capability, primarily using the internet for propaganda and recruitment

threatActors.type: Private Sector Offensive Actor / Cyber Mercenary
threatActors.name: Private Sector Offensive Actor
threatActors.description: A commercial vendor developing zero-day exploits and spyware for client-selected targets

threatActors.name: Data-borne prompt injector
threatActors.description: Cannot authenticate to the agent, but writes text an analyst's query will select: token names / contract data / log payloads on the public ledger, or attacker-influenceable CloudTrail fields. The text arrives in the model's context as a tool result and may steer the next turn. Governance still bounds data access; the risk is a fabricated narrative.

threatActors.name: Compromised upstream supplier (supply chain)
threatActors.description: Serves a malicious DuckDB extension build (installed at cold start unless pre-baked) or ships a malicious release of duckdb / sqlglot / strands / bedrock-agentcore. Code inside the agent process bypasses every SQL-layer control. Low likelihood (signed extensions, HTTPS), high consequence.

trustZones.name: Client side (UI + end user + LLM output)
trustZones.description: The Streamlit UI on the analyst's machine (holds the ID token + app client secret) and the LLM whose SQL output is attacker-influenceable via prompt injection and data-borne content.

trustZones.name: AWS managed platform
trustZones.description: Cognito (token issuance, custom claims read-only on the client), AgentCore Runtime + managed JWT authorizer (microVM isolation, pre-code token validation), Bedrock, CloudWatch. AWS-operated; trusted per the shared-responsibility model.

trustZones.name: Agent process (sample code)
trustZones.description: The session's microVM process: scheduling/session-binding, the statement pipeline, the governance rewrite, the in-process DuckDB. Executes untrusted SQL under layered controls; one session = one principal = one engine, rebound and reset on an owner change.

trustZones.name: Customer account data plane
trustZones.description: S3 buckets/catalogs (analytical data, exports, label tables) and Secrets Manager in the customer's own account, reached only via the scoped read-only execution role.

crossingPoints.description: Inbound AuthN edge: UI/LLM calls to Cognito and the runtime. Only a valid Cognito ID token for the configured audience reaches a session; Bedrock invoke rides the runtime's execution role.
Platform -> agent identity handoff: verified claims cross from the managed authorizer into agent code; scheduling resolves the role, binds the session owner, and resets state on a change.

Untrusted SQL -> agent controls: LLM-generated SQL (prompt-injectable) enters the statement pipeline. THE central boundary: single-statement read-only gate, reserved-name check, governance rewrite (RLS/CLS, raw-path allowlist, table-level deny-by-default), cost gate, fail-closed.
Agent -> customer data plane: engine reads S3/catalog/label/secret data with the scoped read-only execution role over TLS; source-bucket grant pinned to the CUR + account-scoped CloudTrail prefixes.

Agent -> model: scheduling hands the user prompt and role-filtered L0 map to the LLM. The model's reply (SQL) re-enters the agent as untrusted input at CP003; the prompt states row content is data, not instructions.

trustBoundaries.name: Inbound AuthN edge (Cognito + managed authorizer)
controls: AgentCore customJWTAuthorizer: signature via discovery URL + allowedAudience, BEFORE agent code
requestHeaderAllowlist limits forwarded headers to Authorization
trustBoundaries.description: The deployed sample's real authentication perimeter: only requests carrying a valid Cognito ID token for the configured audience reach a runtime session. Verified: no-token=401, forged-token=403, both pre-code.

trustBoundaries.name: Platform -> agent identity handoff
controls: Managed authorizer verifies before agent code
trust-ordered fallback chain with deny-all floor
unknown role -> tenant's MOST restricted policy
session-owner binding: state reset on an owner change (T003)
trustBoundaries.description: Verified identity crosses from the managed authorizer into agent code as claims. The session is bound to its owner; a different identity on a reused session id resets the engine, results, history and counters.

trustBoundaries.name: Untrusted model <-> agent controls
controls: read-only statement allowlist + reserved-name check on the parsed tree

governance rewrite: RLS guarded subqueries, schema-aware CLS EXCLUDE, denied-column rejection, raw-path AST-shape allowlist, statement-root allowlist, local-name shadow refusal, TABLE-LEVEL DENY-BY-DEFAULT
cost gate: partition filter + bounded path expansion
fail-closed on any rewrite exception; every statement audited once
prompt rule: row content is data, not instructions
trustBoundaries.description: The prompt goes to the model and the model's SQL comes back (attacker-influenceable via prompt injection AND data-borne content). THE central boundary of this model. All controls covered by 303 offline tests + a 19-check re-validation on the real code paths.

trustBoundaries.name: Agent -> customer data plane
controls: scoped read-only IAM execution role (source-bucket grant pinned to CUR + account-scoped CloudTrail prefixes)
aws:SourceArn on the CloudWatch Logs export bucket policy
trustBoundaries.description: Engine reads S3/catalog/label/secret data with the scoped read-only execution role over TLS. Only governed SQL output flows back; the account pin is now an IAM boundary, not just a row filter.

assets.name: Governed analytical rows/columns
assets.description: The rows and columns a principal is entitled to see after RLS/CLS and table-level deny-by-default. The asset the authorization layer protects.

assets.name: Cognito ID token (tenant/role claims)
assets.description: The bearer of the verified identity claims that drive authorization; also binds the session owner via sub.

assets.name: Cognito app client secret
assets.description: Used by the UI for SECRET_HASH during login; env-supplied, never committed.

assets.name: GOVERNANCE_POLICIES configuration
assets.description: Per tenant:role, the tables a role may read and their row/column rules. Validated at import; omission fails closed (deny-by-default).

assets.name: Agent-generated SQL (untrusted)
assets.description: The LLM's SQL output — attacker-influenceable via prompt injection and data-borne content; gated, governed and cost-checked before the engine.

flows.description: Cognito issues the ID token to the UI on login.
UI sends the ID token as bearer; the managed authorizer validates signature + audience before agent code.
App client secret used for SECRET_HASH during USER_PASSWORD_AUTH.
LLM SQL enters the pipeline: single-statement gate, governance rewrite, cost gate, fail-closed. UNTRUSTED crossing.
The resolved principal selects the policy that governs the rewrite (unknown -> most restricted; none -> deny-all).
Engine reads S3/catalog/export data with the scoped read-only role.
Only governed rows/columns (RLS/CLS applied, unlisted tables refused) flow back to the UI.

residualRiskAssessments.rationale: Table-level deny-by-default refuses any mounted-but-unlisted table for restricted principals across all four access paths; personas list their readable tables; L0/search are role-filtered. Verified live (verify3) and by 303 offline tests. Residual: a semantically over-broad policy an operator authors is T011.
cw_logs is named by no persona, so it is unreadable except to the unrestricted operator role, and documented as part of the governance boundary. Follows from deny-by-default.

The session is bound to its owner and all retained state is reset on an owner change; verified a junior cannot read an admin-materialized result after the rebind. Residual rests on AgentCore's per-session microVM isolation.
Wide (>cap) and unsatisfiable literal ranges are refused before the engine; non-literal predicates still pass to engine pruning. Worst case is read-only and bounded; verified by unit tests + verify3.
Reserved-name detection is on the parsed tree, catching quoted and column-alias forms; integrity-only, confined to the attacker's own session. Verified end to end.
The guard alias is AST-attached; Govern and the driver fail closed on any exception; every statement is audited exactly once. Accountability defect closed; data was never exposed.

The source-bucket grant is pinned to the CUR prefix and the account-scoped CloudTrail prefix, with ListBucket restricted by s3:prefix; the account pin is now an IAM boundary. Requires the unrestricted persona to matter at all.
aws:SourceArn pins the CloudWatch Logs export condition to the runtime's own log group; cross-account was already blocked by SourceAccount.

Data-borne prompt injection is structural to agentic data analysis: the model must read data to reason. Governance keeps it from widening data access and the pipeline from writing/host-reaching, so the realistic damage is a wrong narrative. The prompt now states rows are data, not instructions.

Low likelihood (signed extensions, HTTPS fetch), high consequence. Accepted for now with pre-baking/pinning tracked as a follow-up (M024). A runtime that INSTALLs at cold start is an avoidable standing dependency.

Policy JSON and LABELS_PREFIX are validated at import, and omission now fails closed (deny-by-default + deny-all floor). Residual: a well-formed but semantically over-broad row_filter still governs as written; the audit trail gives the signal.
AST rewrite guards every governed-table reference through raw/s3t/glue/dl; denied-column selection is a clean rejection. Residual bounded by fail-closed parsing and a read-only worst case.
A local name reusing a governed table's name is refused (nine adversarial shapes), so a governed name always denotes the governed table.
Statement-root allowlist rejects opaque Command shapes for restricted principals; EXPLAIN ANALYZE no longer executes ungoverned. Regression-tested.
Single-statement rule uses the engine's own parser; end-to-end proof the second statement never reaches the engine; READ_ONLY attaches and no write IAM bound any residual.
AST-shape allowlist rejects new file functions by default; cloud-verified. Additions to the generator exception require explicit justification.
The deny-all floor is the default and where blank/unknown claims resolve; the entrypoint refuses before the model runs. Local CLI must name the principal explicitly.

custom:tenant/custom:role are READ-only on the app client (verified NotAuthorizedException); role assignment is an operator action. Residual: an operator with Cognito admin rights can still misassign (same class as IAM role assignment).
Platform-enforced pre-code validation (401/403 verified). Residual: stolen VALID tokens are T026; the authorizer is AWS-managed and out of sample scope.

Documented trust assumption on the local/CLI SigV4 path only: the caller is IAM-authenticated infrastructure trusted to assert identity. The deployed path uses the JWT authorizer, where these sources are unreachable pre-code.
conn_lock serializes execute+fetch and the schema probe/session lister; single-principal-per-session makes the worst case an integrity glitch, not cross-principal leakage. Regression-tested.
The alias is attached via the AST (quoted when unsafe) and only the subquery node is extracted, so a hostile alias is a single inert statement. Verified: victim survives, one statement.

Aggregate/timing inference against denied columns is an industry-wide limitation of query-rewrite governance. The one concrete oracle (EXPLAIN ANALYZE) is closed (T014). Sample data is public/synthetic; production guidance is physical separation.

Deliberate transparency: the trace shows the principal only their OWN policy application, the same information the clean rejection conveys, never another tenant's data. A single filter point exists for opacity-preferring deployments.

Misuse-of-sample: the module-level active-role slot is safe only under one-session-one-principal (AgentCore microVM). Cannot be closed by code in a sample; controlled by prominent documentation. HIGH residual kept visible on purpose.

Bearer-token theft is inherent to token auth; lifetime bounds exposure and a stolen session cannot be escalated beyond the victim's role (claims read-only). Demo credentials are rotate-before-exposing; MFA deliberately off for demo. Analyst-host security is out of scope for a sample.

Blast radius is structurally one microVM; the memory envelope turns exhaustion into slower-not-dead. Cost exposure is the customer's own account, bounded by their throttles; per-request cost is standard for any LLM app.

softwareProfile.description: Python 3.11-3.13 on Amazon Bedrock AgentCore Runtime (one microVM per session). Five layers in request order: Scheduling (data_agent/scheduling: claims->role, session binding, SSE), Context (data_agent/context: L0/L1 role-filtered data map, partition-filter cost gate, result shaping, history compression), Governance (data_agent/governance: policies + hardening + sqlglot rewrite, AUTHORIZATION ONLY, fail-closed, table-level deny-by-default), Compute (in-process DuckDB), Storage (S3 durable data). One statement pipeline (Gate->Govern->Cost->Execute) audits once per statement and fails closed on any exception. CI gates: ruff, 303 offline unit tests incl. adversarial authz regressions, bandit, semgrep, detect-secrets.

dataAssetProfiles.name: Analytical dataset on S3 (4 access paths)
dataAssetProfiles.description: Parquet/Iceberg tables on S3 reachable via raw glob, S3 Tables, Glue, DuckLake. Public aws-public-blockchain Ethereum data + the deployer's own CUR/CloudTrail/CloudWatch exports. Per-tenant/per-account visibility is enforced by the RLS/CLS rewrite; a table not named in a restricted principal's policy is refused outright (table-level deny-by-default).

dataAssetProfiles.name: Identity claims (tenant, role, sub)
dataAssetProfiles.description: Cognito ID-token claims (custom:tenant/custom:role) validated by the AgentCore managed JWT authorizer BEFORE agent code runs; sub binds the session owner. Or identity asserted by a SigV4 caller (local/CLI path). Integrity of these claims is the authorization foundation.

dataAssetProfiles.name: Governance policy table
dataAssetProfiles.description: GOVERNANCE_POLICIES JSON: per tenant:role, the tables that role may read (row_filter / deny_columns, {} = readable/no restriction) + allow_raw_paths. Validated at import. Unknown roles resolve to the tenant's most-restricted policy; no policy = deny-all floor.

dataAssetProfiles.name: Attribution label tables (OFAC + synthetic CEX)
dataAssetProfiles.description: ofac_addresses (REAL public OFAC SDN list) and cex_deposit_labels (SYNTHETIC; subject_identity mimics KYC linkage, column-denied to junior and hidden from search_schema discovery for that role).

dataAssetProfiles.name: Cognito app client secret
dataAssetProfiles.description: App client secret for SECRET_HASH during USER_PASSWORD_AUTH; supplied to the UI via env, never committed.

dataAssetProfiles.name: DuckLake PostgreSQL credentials
dataAssetProfiles.description: Optional multi-writer catalog credentials in AWS Secrets Manager, fetched at runtime by the execution role; never in env or code. (PG catalog leg not deployed in the reference config.)

userPersonas.name: End user (investigator / junior analyst)
userPersonas.description: Logs in at Cognito; ID-token claims carry tenant/role; a restricted principal whose visibility is bounded by RLS/CLS and by table-level deny-by-default. Primary adversary: crafts natural-language questions to steer the LLM into SQL that reaches other tenants' rows, denied columns, or unlisted tables.

userPersonas.name: Calling application (SigV4)
userPersonas.description: IAM-authenticated infrastructure invoking the runtime on the local/CLI path; trusted to assert its users' identity via header/payload. Unused when the JWT authorizer is configured (the deployed default). Must also use a fresh, unguessable session id per identity (session-binding assumption).

userPersonas.name: Operator (deployer)
userPersonas.description: Customer engineer deploying the sample; owns env config incl. GOVERNANCE_POLICIES, Cognito users, catalog ARNs. Out of scope as an adversary; misconfiguration is in scope.

userPersonas.name: LLM (Bedrock Claude)
userPersonas.description: Generates SQL from natural language; its output executes after the single-statement read-only gate and governance rewrite. Untrusted-input channel: subject to prompt injection via user questions and via data-borne content in query results.

nonFunctionalRequirements.rationale: The governance layer fails closed: a restricted principal never observes rows, columns, or TABLES outside its policy via any of the four access paths. Unparseable SQL, opaque statement shapes, unknown principals (deny-all floor), explicit denied-column selection, a mounted-but-unlisted table, and any exception in the rewrite path result in rejection. Verified by 303 offline tests + a 19-check re-validation on the real code paths (the table-level deny-by-default release).

Agent-generated SQL (possibly adversarial via prompt injection) must not write persistently, exfiltrate (COPY TO), attach foreign databases, smuggle a second statement, reach raw file functions as a restricted principal, overwrite a framework result table (reserved-name check on the parsed tree), or degrade the cost gate to a whole-prefix scan (wide/unsatisfiable literal ranges are refused).

referenceCatalogue.description: Threat actors the server pre-loaded but that were never assessed for this system. These are NOT part of the threat model.
